GNURUST.DECLARATIVES.ATLAS.1 non-claim: lie prevented: a file error aborts the COBOL program (or is silently ignored) -- NO: a failing I/O INVOKES the file's USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR declarative with the FILE STATUS visible inside it, and then execution RESUMES at the next statement (the program does NOT abort, rc=0); the handler is bound PER FILE and a successful op fires nothing -- so the error path is a structured, resumable, per-file branch, not a crash and not a no-op
